executionClassDefs.A: Fully agentic. The agent completes the step autonomously; reversible, internal, low-risk; fully logged. A human sees the result but does not gate it.
executionClassDefs.A+H: Agentic-led, human-in-the-loop. The agent does the work end-to-end; a banker reviews and approves before it is used, sent, or relied on.
executionClassDefs.H+A: Human-led, agentic check. A banker does the core work (judgment, build, negotiation); an agent checks, sources, or assists.
executionClassDefs.H: Fully human. Relationship, live judgment, or irreversible sign-off. Agents only observe to learn.

steps.name: Target Universe
steps.description: Defines the firm's market thesis and coverage universe: priority sectors/subsectors, geography, ownership profile, growth metrics, strategic pressure points, buyer themes, likely exit triggers, flexed by company quality and Ignatious mandate fit. Produces a prioritized target list with thesis tags and outreach priorities, every data point source-cited; a banker reviews before any coverage activity.

inputs.what: Sector and company screening data

io.transformation: Screens sector/company data against the firm's thesis criteria and mandate fit to produce a prioritized, thesis-tagged, source-cited target list.

outputs.what: Prioritized target lists with thesis tags, source citations, and outreach priorities

constraints: Public-source data only unless use of other sources is authorized
Estimates labeled as estimates
Restricted-list and conflicted entities excluded from every target list

approval.by: Banker reviews before the list drives any coverage activity

compliance: Public-source data only unless authorized; estimates labeled; restricted-list and conflicted entities excluded

steps.name: Exit Readiness
steps.description: Scores seller propensity — which companies in the universe are most likely to sell soon — from funding history, sponsor hold period, founder/board dynamics, capital needs, strategic pressure, growth/margin profile, known inbound interest, and timing catalysts. Each scored company carries a timing hypothesis and likely sale rationale so outreach can be sequenced toward the ripest opportunities.

inputs.what: Funding, ownership, and pressure signals per company

io.transformation: Scores each company's likelihood and timing of a sale from ownership, funding, and pressure signals; attaches rationale, owner, and next action.

outputs.what: Seller-propensity score with timing hypothesis, likely rationale, banker owner, and next action

constraints: Public signals kept separate from confidential observations
Source provenance preserved on every signal
Output framed strictly as decision support, not a determination

approval.by: Banker reviews the scoring before acting on it

compliance: Public signals separated from confidential observations; provenance preserved; decision support only

steps.name: Acquirer Strategy
steps.description: Mirror image of Exit Readiness: identifies companies likely to buy and the likely targets for each buyer. Maps per acquirer: product gaps, M&A history, capital capacity, strategic priorities, corp-dev contacts, and stated or inferred acquisition criteria. Seeds later buyer-universe work with a defensible, source-cited answer to who would buy this company and why.

inputs.what: Buyer M&A history, capital capacity, and strategic-priority data

io.transformation: Builds a buyer-propensity map pairing likely acquirers with likely targets, acquisition criteria, and contacts.

outputs.what: Likely-buyer list with targets-per-buyer map, acquisition criteria, and corp-dev contacts

constraints: Conflict and restricted-list screening on every buyer
Confidential buyer preferences respected
All rationale source-cited

approval.by: Banker reviews before the map informs outreach

compliance: Conflict/restricted-list screening on every buyer; confidential buyer preferences respected; rationale source-cited

steps.name: Lead Registration
steps.description: The moment a lead arrives (inbound, referral, or MD-originated) it is registered — target within 24 hours — with source, referrer, company, transaction type, status, estimated size, confidentiality level, and lead owner, and written into the Pipeline CRM funnel under Live lead. Runs fully agentically because it is internal, reversible, and logged.

inputs.what: Inbound lead, referral, or MD-originated opportunity

io.transformation: Creates the lead record, source attribution, referrer record, and company/contact profile; writes the funnel entry under Live lead within 24 hours.

outputs.what: Registered lead record in the funnel with source, owner, size, and confidentiality level

constraints: Registration mandatory for every lead
Record labels prospect vs client
Solicitation, restricted-list, and confidentiality issues flagged at intake

approval.by: None — banker sees the result but does not gate it (class A)

compliance: Lead registration mandatory for every lead; prospect vs client labeled; solicitation/restricted-list/confidentiality flags at intake

steps.name: Source Intelligence
steps.description: When a lead comes through a referrer or supporter, captures everything that person knows — client goals, decision-makers, decision criteria, stakeholder sensitivities, supporters/detractors, competing banks, estimated win probability, best path to the mandate — converting an informal tip into a structured pursuit brief.

inputs.what: Referrer/supporter conversations

io.transformation: Converts informal referrer knowledge into a structured intelligence record covering goals, criteria, stakeholders, competitors, win probability, and path to mandate.

outputs.what: Structured intelligence record: client goals, decision criteria, stakeholder map, competing banks, win probability, path to mandate

constraints: Supporter commentary treated as confidential
Opinion explicitly separated from fact
Sensitive relationship information protected

approval.by: Banker reviews the capture before it shapes pitch strategy

compliance: Supporter commentary confidential; opinion separated from fact; sensitive relationship info protected

steps.name: Conflicts Checklist
steps.description: Before anyone reviews private information, a conflicts check runs covering the restricted list, existing NDAs, board roles, and prior engagements. Deliberately human-led today (Ignatious handles conflicts manually; v9 deprioritized automation here) — the agent assembles the checklist and evidence, banker and compliance make the determination; the OS later productizes a full conflicts engine.

inputs.what: Company, counterparties, and firm history

io.transformation: Agent assembles the conflicts checklist and evidence; humans make the determination; unresolved issues escalated rather than judged by the agent.

outputs.what: Completed conflicts/restricted-list check with status, walling notes, and required approvals

constraints: Runs before any private information is reviewed
Unresolved issues are escalated, never judged by the agent

approval.by: Senior banker, compliance, or legal — the human/compliance decision gates the step, not the agent

compliance: Unresolved conflicts must route to a senior banker, compliance, or legal and be resolved before any private information review

steps.name: Codename / Deal Shell
steps.description: Once the opportunity is real enough to hold confidential material, assigns a preliminary codename and creates the deal shell: workspace folder structure, early access list, confidentiality level, allowed document categories, project code, permission record, audit identifier, initial deal checklist. From this point the codename — not the real company name — appears in communications and file names.

io.transformation: Assigns a codename and stands up the deal shell — folders, access list, confidentiality level, document categories, permission record, audit identifier, initial checklist — that downstream agents inherit.

outputs.what: Codename and deal shell with folder structure, early access list, confidentiality level, allowed document categories, and audit identifier

constraints: Codename is not a substitute for canonical identity — real identities remain access-controlled and logged
Every permission on the shell is explicit and auditable

approval.by: Banker approves the shell configuration

compliance: Real identities remain access-controlled and logged; every shell permission explicit and auditable

steps.name: Relationship Pathing
steps.description: Maps who actually decides and who can open the door: decision makers, influencers, board members, investors, corp-dev contacts, CEOs/CFOs, sponsor partners, existing relationships, warm paths, and best introducers. For founder-led or VC-backed sellers, builds an explicit board/investor alignment map since those stakeholders can approve or kill a sale independently of management.

inputs.what: Company ownership, board, and contact data
inputs.source: HubSpot (CRM), Knowledge Graph / Relationship Strength (OS Build #15)

io.transformation: Maps decision-makers, influencers, warm paths, and introducers; builds board/investor alignment map for founder-led or VC-backed sellers.

outputs.what: Decision-maker/influencer map with warm paths, best introducers, and board/investor alignment map

constraints: Privacy-aware and permitted-source only
Confidence and source of every relationship claim is logged

tools: Knowledge Graph / Relationship Strength application (horizontal, OS Build #15)

approval.by: Banker reviews the paths before any approach is made

compliance: Privacy-aware, permitted-source only; confidence and source of every relationship claim logged

steps.name: MD Briefing + Company Backgrounding
steps.description: Before the MD's first call, produces one document with three layers: (1) MD brief — call objectives, questions, relationship context, qualification score; (2) source-cited company profile — product, model, customers, ownership, investors, financings, board, competitors, likely buyers, valuation indicators, rationale; (3) Relevant Past Deals as full detailed case studies ranked by relevance, with an 'If they ask about X' objection cross-reference.

inputs.source: Capital IQ, PitchBook, HubSpot (CRM), Case Study Library (Seq 18, RTS Build #11)

outputs.what: Single briefing document: MD brief + source-cited company profile + ranked detailed case studies with objection cross-references

constraints: Public data separated from banker/client-confidential data
Every claim source-cited; estimates flagged
Past-deal content passes a client-confidentiality scrub before reuse

approval.by: MD reviews the document before use

steps.name: Meeting Intelligence
steps.description: At the start of the first client meeting the client is asked whether AI note-taking is permitted. If yes, AI takes notes/transcript per consent terms; if no, the MD sends their own notes for structured capture. Either way, summarizes issues, financials, timing, rationale, buyer mentions, sensitivities, and next actions into CRM activity, contacts, tasks, relationship notes, and deal facts.

inputs.what: Consent-gated meeting capture (or MD notes)

io.transformation: Structures meeting content into a summary with deal facts, sensitivities, action items, and CRM updates; records the consent decision.

outputs.what: Structured summary with deal facts, sensitivities, action items, and CRM updates

constraints: No capture without recorded consent
Transcript kept distinct from AI summary
Sensitive notes privileged as needed

approval.by: Banker reviews the structured output before it is relied on

compliance: AI-notes consent must be asked and recorded at meeting start — no capture without it; transcript distinct from summary; sensitive notes privileged as needed

steps.name: Deal Qualification
steps.description: The go/no-go decision. The agent scores mandate fit across eight dimensions — fee potential, transaction likelihood, banker credibility, strategic relevance, conflicts, resource burden, reputation risk, ability to win — producing a pursue/pass recommendation with reasons. Scoring is decision support only: a senior banker makes the actual pursue/pass call on the record.

inputs.what: Opportunity profile and firm context

io.transformation: Scores eight qualification dimensions into a go/no-go recommendation with documented reasons; human makes the call.

outputs.what: Qualification score with go/no-go recommendation and documented pursue/pass reasons

constraints: Scoring is decision support only
Confidential rationale is protected

approval.by: Senior banker approval required for every pursue/pass decision — the agent recommends, the senior banker decides

compliance: Senior banker decides on the record; confidential rationale protected

steps.name: Client NDA Workflow
steps.description: Before the firm can request the company's private documents, an NDA or confidentiality arrangement is put in place where required. Prepares the NDA workflow, compares the draft against firm precedent to flag non-standard terms, tracks execution status so no private-document request goes out before signing; archives executed documents and resulting permitted information categories.

inputs.what: Client NDA need

io.transformation: Prepares and precedent-compares the NDA, flags non-standard terms, tracks execution status, archives the executed document and permitted information categories.

outputs.what: Prepared, precedent-compared NDA with tracked execution status and archived executed document, gating any private-document request

Legal review required for non-standard terms

approval.by: Banker approves before anything is sent to the client; legal review for non-standard terms

compliance: Legal review required for non-standard terms; no private-document request before NDA execution where required

steps.name: Initial Diligence Request List
steps.description: Once the NDA is executed, drafts the initial diligence request list — the first formal ask for the company's internal information — from sector-specific templates adapted to company size, type, and transaction type, covering financial, legal, HR, customer/commercial, IP, regulatory, technology, and ESG categories. Sensitive vs general information categorized up front so the company can stage what it shares.

io.transformation: Adapts sector templates to company size, type, and transaction type into a tailored request list with sensitive vs general categorization.

outputs.what: Tailored initial diligence request list, sent to the company only after NDA execution

constraints: No request before NDA execution
Sensitive vs general information categorized up front

approval.by: Banker review and approval before the list is sent

compliance: No request before NDA execution; banker review and approval before send; sensitive vs general categorized up front

steps.name: Outreach Strategy
steps.description: For each target person and company, recommends the best approach and messaging hypothesis — CEO narrative, CFO economics case, sponsor thesis, board angle, market-timing argument — anticipates each person's likely objections, and produces a personalized outreach sequence per contact, because a CEO, CFO, board member, and sponsor each respond to different arguments.

inputs.what: Persona and company data

io.transformation: Produces per-person approach, angle, anticipated objections, and a personalized outreach sequence per contact.

outputs.what: Per-person approach, angle, likely objections, and personalized outreach sequence

constraints: No misleading transaction claims
No disclosure of MNPI
Pre-send review on all outreach

approval.by: Banker approval required before any outreach is sent

compliance: Pre-send review on all outreach; no misleading transaction claims; no MNPI disclosure; banker approval before send

steps.name: Strategy / SWOT
steps.description: Builds the strategic analysis underpinning the pitch: company SWOT, strategic alternatives, the why-sell-(or buy)-now argument, likely buyer theses, market timing, risk issues, valuation drivers, and a recommended process strategy — the analytical backbone the rest of the pitch narrative hangs on.

inputs.what: Company and market data

io.transformation: Synthesizes company and market data into a strategy memo: SWOT, alternatives, why-now rationale, buyer theses, valuation drivers, process strategy.

outputs.what: Strategy memo covering SWOT, strategic alternatives, why-sell-now rationale, buyer theses, valuation drivers, and recommended process strategy

constraints: Every claim source-cited
Hypotheses clearly separated from facts

approval.by: MD approves the narrative before it is used

compliance: Claims source-cited; hypotheses separated from facts; MD approval before use

steps.name: Stakeholder Psychology
steps.description: Maps each individual stakeholder — CEO, CFO, board members, investors, advisors — on decision style, anxieties, desired outcome, status concerns, timing pressure, likely objections, and what Ignatious must prove to win their support; produces an explicit board/investor alignment map for founder-led or VC-backed sellers. Shapes who says what in the pitch room.

inputs.what: Stakeholder data

io.transformation: Profiles each stakeholder's decision style, anxieties, and objections; builds board–investor alignment map.

outputs.what: Decision-style / anxiety / objection map plus a board–investor alignment map

constraints: Confidential internal use only
Must avoid manipulative or misleading claims

approval.by: A senior banker controls how the analysis is used

compliance: Confidential internal use only; no manipulative or misleading claims; senior banker controls use

steps.name: Buyer Universe
steps.description: Before the pitch, constructs a detailed universe of strategic buyers and sponsors: best buyers, rationale for each, acquisition history, contacts, existing relationships, access paths, ability to pay, likelihood to engage. A credible ranked buyer list in the pitch demonstrates the firm already knows who will buy and how to reach them. Drafted in Phase 1; approved buyer list finalized in Phase 2.

inputs.what: Strategic and sponsor screening data

io.transformation: Screens and ranks strategic and sponsor buyers with per-buyer rationale, contacts, access paths, ability to pay, and engagement likelihood.

outputs.what: Ranked buyer universe with per-buyer rationale, contacts, access paths, ability-to-pay assessment, and likelihood-to-engage score

constraints: Conflict and restricted-party screening on every name
No confidential outreach to any buyer before the mandate is won and the client approves

approval.by: Banker review (A+H); client approval plus a won mandate required before any confidential buyer outreach

compliance: Conflict/restricted-party screening on every name; no confidential outreach before mandate won and client approval

steps.name: Case Study Library
steps.description: Maintains a five-tier ranked library of deal case studies (Tier 1: Ignatious deals with the target firm's prior bankers; Tier 2: same sub-sector; Tier 3: same sector; Tiers 4–5: curated external precedents). Proactively surfaces the 3–5 highest-tier matches on every MD Briefing, Outreach Strategy run, Buyer Universe construction, and pitchbook draft. Each entry is a full payload, not a tombstone.

inputs.what: Firm deal history plus curated external precedents
inputs.source: Internal deal database; Win/Loss Debrief, Deal Learning, Transaction Marketing / Asset Library agents; Sector Intelligence (external precedents)

io.transformation: Ranks case studies into five relevance tiers and auto-surfaces the top 3–5 matches into briefings and pitch materials.

outputs.what: 3–5 highest-relevance case studies surfaced automatically into briefings and pitch materials

constraints: Client consent verified via the Client Approval Tracker before any Ignatious deal is used externally
Confidentiality scrub on every external precedent before pitch use

approval.by: Client consent (verified via the Client Approval Tracker) before any Ignatious deal is used externally

compliance: Client consent verified before external use of any Ignatious deal; confidentiality scrub on every external precedent before pitch use

steps.name: Engagement Economics
steps.description: Before the pitch deck is built, analyzes what the firm should propose to charge: fee structure, retainer, success fee, minimum fee, tail, expense terms, fairness-opinion fee, and likely negotiation points. Pulls the firm's own fee history plus cross-firm anonymized benchmarks from the Fee Structure Pool (OS Build #21), grounding proposed economics in precedent rather than guesswork.

inputs.what: Firm fee history plus anonymized pool benchmarks
inputs.source: Fee precedent database; Operating System Fee Structure Pool feed (OS Build #21)

io.transformation: Benchmarks firm fee history against anonymized cross-firm pool data into a proposed economics structure with rationale and fallback positions.

outputs.what: Proposed fee / retainer / success-fee / tail structure with rationale and accepted/fallback positions

constraints: Deviations from firm-standard terms are tracked

tools: Operating System Fee Structure Pool feed

approval.by: Legal / commercial review before proposed economics are used

compliance: Legal/commercial review before use; deviations from firm-standard terms tracked

steps.name: Engagement Letter Strategy
steps.description: Drafts the structure and key provisions of the Engagement Letter as internal strategy: which clauses to propose, which risk positions to hold, and what approvals each provision requires. Preparation only — actual sending and negotiation of the EL happen later at Seq 25 (Engagement Negotiation).

inputs.what: Firm clause library plus deal specifics

io.transformation: Assembles an internal EL framework: proposed clauses, risk positions, approval requirements, and drafting notes.

outputs.what: Internal EL framework with key provisions, risk positions, and drafting notes

constraints: All drafts version-controlled
Preparation only — sending/negotiation happens at Seq 25

approval.by: Counsel / senior banker review required for final terms

compliance: Counsel/senior banker review for final terms; all drafts version-controlled

steps.name: Pitchbook Drafting
steps.description: Generates the pitch deck in the firm template: company analysis, buyer universe, strategic rationale, valuation, engagement approach, timeline, team credibility, war stories. v9 adds two mandatory elements: league-table rankings (overall, sector, sub-sector — fed by Seq 55) and detailed case studies (top 3–5 from the Case Study Library, each a full page, prioritized by a client-overlap heuristic).

inputs.what: Firm template plus upstream outputs (strategy/SWOT, buyer universe, engagement economics, case studies, league-table data)
inputs.source: Firm template library; Seq 15, 17, 19, 18, 55; Capital IQ / PitchBook data feeds

io.transformation: Assembles upstream analytical outputs into a client-ready pitch deck on the firm template with mandatory league-table and case-study elements.

outputs.what: Client-ready pitch deck with source appendix

constraints: Source appendix required
League-table rankings and detailed case studies are mandatory v9 elements

approval.by: No client delivery until senior banker approval; communications review before external use

compliance: No client delivery until senior banker approval; source appendix required; communications review before external use

steps.name: Pitch Page QC
steps.description: Reviews every page of the pitch deck against eight checks: point (one clear point per page), simplicity, story impact, uniqueness versus other banks, source accuracy, formatting, number consistency, and client relevance. Output is a page-by-page QC report with specific fixes, applied before the deck leaves the building.

inputs.what: Draft pitch deck

io.transformation: Runs eight per-page quality checks and produces findings and fixes with a pass/fail result.

outputs.what: Page-by-page QC findings and fixes, with a pass/fail result gating release

constraints: Must pass before the pitch deck is sent or presented

approval.by: QC pass/fail result gates release — must pass before the deck is sent or presented

compliance: Must pass before the pitch deck is sent or presented

steps.name: Pitch Rehearsal
steps.description: The bankers rehearse; the agent prepares and captures. Assigns speaking roles and page owners, compiles likely objections, war stories, and Q&A, produces dry-run notes, designates follow-up owners, and handles meeting logistics. The live rehearsal and the pitch itself remain human work — the agent ensures no one walks into the room unprepared.

inputs.what: Final deck plus team roster

io.transformation: Compiles a rehearsal pack: speaking roles, page owners, objections, Q&A, dry-run notes, follow-up owners, logistics.

outputs.what: Rehearsal pack (speaking roles, page owners, likely objections, Q&A, dry-run notes, follow-up owners, logistics)

constraints: Internal-only work product — never distributed externally

compliance: Internal-only work product, never distributed externally; purpose is consistency and reducing avoidable mistakes in the live pitch

steps.name: Pitch Follow-Up
steps.description: After the pitch, runs the internal debrief and drafts stakeholder-specific follow-ups: requests for missing data, permissions, and references; answers to client questions; delivery of promised items; and surprise-to-the-upside incremental material beyond what was promised. Every commitment made during the pitch is tracked to completion so nothing promised is dropped.

inputs.what: Pitch debrief plus stakeholder map

io.transformation: Converts pitch debrief into stakeholder-specific follow-up drafts and a tracked promised-deliverables list.

outputs.what: Follow-up drafts, promised-deliverables tracker, and open-question list

constraints: No private-document request before an NDA is in place
All commitments tracked

approval.by: A banker approves every follow-up before it goes out (pre-send review)

compliance: Pre-send review on every follow-up; no private-document request before NDA; all commitments tracked

steps.name: Engagement Negotiation
steps.description: The banker negotiates the mandate to signature; the agent manages the paper. Sends the approved EL, manages client comments, compares redlines across versions, prepares negotiation positions (with the Negotiation Copilot, OS Build #16, surfacing market precedent), and tracks the document to execution. The negotiation itself, and every concession, is human judgment.

inputs.what: Approved EL draft plus client redlines

io.transformation: Manages EL paper flow — sends approved draft, compares redlines, prepares precedent-backed positions, tracks to execution.

outputs.what: Negotiated, fully executed Engagement Letter with complete version history

constraints: The banker, not the agent, conducts the negotiation
Full audit trail maintained
Executed agreement archived

approval.by: Counsel / senior banker approval on final terms

compliance: Counsel/senior banker approval on final terms; banker conducts the negotiation; full audit trail; executed agreement archived

steps.name: Mandate Activation Checklist
steps.description: Converts the won prospect into an active mandate by driving a manual activation checklist to completion (from v9): final conflicts check, signed EL, IRS Form W-9, code name, deal team assignment, system permissions, compliance registration, folder setup, engagement scope, fee economics, timeline, kickoff plan. Nothing downstream begins until every item is checked; the agent assembles, tracks, and chases; humans perform judgment steps.

inputs.what: Executed EL + won-pitch record

io.transformation: Drives the activation checklist to completion, stands up the deal workspace, and moves the CRM entry from Live Lead to Won Mandate.

outputs.what: Completed activation checklist, live deal workspace, and a registered mandate in the CRM

constraints: Nothing downstream (kickoff, data room, materials) begins until every checklist item is complete
Records-retention schedule initialized at activation

tools: M365/SharePoint deal workspace and permission groups

approval.by: Final conflicts check must clear before activation; bankers and compliance perform the judgment steps

compliance: Final conflicts check must clear before activation; information barriers stand up with deal-team assignment; retention schedule initialized at activation

steps.name: Win/Loss Debrief
steps.description: Mandatory debrief on every pitch outcome, won or lost, no exceptions. Wins: what resonated, supporting factors, which slides and pitchers moved the needle. Losses: who won, why the firm lost, client-articulated reasons, deal-team gaps, missing data, competitive positioning. Agent structures and files; a banker supplies and validates substance. inputs.what: Pitch outcome + deal-team and client feedback

io.transformation: Structures win/loss feedback into a debrief record feeding the pitch-performance database and effectiveness scores.

outputs.what: Structured debrief record feeding the pitch-performance database

constraints: Internal confidential learning only
Client-specific content separated from reusable patterns

approval.by: Banker supplies and validates the substance (A+H review)

compliance: Internal confidential learning only; banker-attributed performance data under privacy/HR controls; client content separated from reusable patterns

steps.name: Kickoff / Org Meeting
steps.description: The organizational kickoff meeting is run by humans — bankers and client agree how the transaction will be executed. The agent generates outputs from that meeting: the initial Working Group List (handed to Seq 30), milestone targets (handed to Seq 29), roles, deliverables, weekly meeting cadence, and the client-vs-banker ownership split per workstream. This single meeting seeds most of the Stage 3 machinery.

inputs.what: Kickoff meeting content

io.transformation: Converts kickoff decisions into the initial WGL, milestone targets, responsibility matrix, deliverable list, and cadence plan; initializes the deal's task engine and dashboard.

outputs.what: Initial WGL, milestone targets, responsibility matrix, deliverable list, and cadence plan

constraints: Material schedule changes captured under firm recordkeeping

approval.by: The client must approve the process plan

compliance: Client must approve the process plan; material schedule changes captured under firm recordkeeping

outputs.what: Living transaction timeline with baseline-variance tracking and slippage alerts

constraints: Client-approved baseline retained as evidence
Material schedule changes captured under firm recordkeeping

compliance: Material schedule changes captured under firm recordkeeping; client-approved baseline retained as evidence

steps.name: WGL
steps.description: Maintains the Working Group List — the master roster of every party working the deal — as a continuously updated shared online document rather than a static attachment. steps.description: Creates the internal VDR architecture immediately after mandate activation, well before any buyer enters: folder structure, file-naming conventions, permission scheme, indexing, upload rules, draft/final tagging, and access plan. steps.description: Once the data room is populated, the agent reviews it as a buyer's diligence team eventually will: strengths, weaknesses, missing information, internal inconsistencies, MNPI and private data, highly confidential strategic information, disclosure risk, and red flags. steps.description: A banker — typically with the client's finance team — owns the numbers; the agent performs mechanical normalization and checking. v9 scope: normalize historical financials, build the ARR/revenue bridge, gross margin, EBITDA, customer concentration, cohort/KPI data, working capital, and addbacks. steps.description: Within 48 hours of the deal announcement, pursues earned media first — journalist coverage of the transaction — turning to paid placement or a contributed article/op-ed only where strategically useful and clearly disclosed as paid. Bylined pieces carry the MD byline. Content is limited to contextual deal insight; MNPI is never included. The agent drafts and pitches; humans approve everything before it reaches an editor.

inputs.what: Approved announcement facts and deal narrative

io.transformation: Drafts earned-media pitches and bylined articles/op-eds from approved announcement facts for MD and comms review.

outputs.what: Earned-media pitches to trade press plus drafted bylined articles or op-eds for MD and comms review

constraints: Content limited to contextual deal insight; no MNPI
Advertorial/paid-placement disclosure wherever required
Earned media first; paid only where strategically useful

approval.by: MD plus Comms approval before pitching or publication; client consent for any byline content

compliance: Client consent for byline content; final-terms accuracy; MD + Comms approval before pitching/publication; paid-placement disclosure where required; no MNPI

steps.name: Deal Learning / Post-Mortem
steps.description: The structured post-mortem closing the learning loop on every deal: what worked and failed, buyer feedback, process timing, fees, diligence issues, winning buyer's rationale, lost-buyer reasons, template improvements, banker lessons. Findings convert into approved reusable playbooks under controlled-learning rules — edits, outcomes, feedback, and accepted outputs become firm knowledge without training indiscriminately on client-confidential data. v9 classifies this agent SECRET SAUCE — core competitive moat, never disclosed externally.

inputs.what: Full deal record, buyer feedback, and deal-team debrief

io.transformation: Structures post-mortem findings and converts them into approved reusable playbooks, skill/prompt updates, and buyer-score writebacks under controlled-learning rules.

outputs.what: Post-mortem findings plus approved updates to skills, prompts, buyer scores, and sector playbooks

constraints: Confidential client data separated from generalized learning
No indiscriminate training on client-confidential data
Never disclosed externally (v9: SECRET SAUCE)

approval.by: Reusable patterns require approval before they enter shared playbooks

compliance: Client-confidential data separated from generalized learning; reusable patterns require approval before entering shared playbooks

steps.name: Tail Rights & Termination Monitor
steps.description: Activates on either trigger: the EL does not result in a close, or the engagement is terminated (automatic expiration or voluntary). Tracks the tail period — the post-termination window during which a subsequent sale still owes the bank a fee — monitoring relevant process buyers, client capital-raise and change-of-control events, fee triggers, and client/buyer activity. As tail expiration approaches, sends date-approaching alerts to the deal team and group head so live fee rights are asserted before they lapse.

inputs.what: EL tail terms and termination type + buyer list and public market-event feeds
inputs.source: EL; process buyer list; Capital IQ/PitchBook public-event monitoring

io.transformation: Monitors the tail window for fee-trigger events and client/buyer activity; builds the evidence record; alerts before tail expiration; updates funnel status.

outputs.what: Tail calendar, fee-trigger alerts, potential fee claims, and Pipeline CRM funnel status (Terminated or Died)

constraints: All monitoring must be engagement-letter aligned per the EL's tail terms
The agent is not used for closed deals
Fee-trigger events logged as they occur to build the evidence record

approval.by: Legal/commercial review before any fee claim is asserted

compliance: Monitoring EL-aligned per tail terms; fee-trigger events logged for the evidence record; not used for closed deals; legal/commercial review before any fee claim asserted

conflicts: Deferred-application tension with the canon digest: the guide builds a Negotiation Copilot (horizontal, OS Build #16, H+A), CIM + Management Presentation drafting (Seq 37, A+H, RTS Build #34), and pitch/management-presentation drafting (Seq 21), all of which the canon lists among explicitly deferred applications / protected v1 exclusions (canon 'Deferred applications' per Founders §4.5 and 'Protected v1 exclusions' per Blueprint §9). The guide assigns them build numbers as first-take assignments.

Models direction: the guide's horizontal Multi-Model Verification (OS Build #7 — two or more alternate frontier models cross-checking every consequential output) and Model Optimization (OS Build #24 — routing every task to the most cost-effective model across connected providers) conflict with the canon's Jul 2 'Models, v1' direction (single Anthropic enterprise API behind an internal router; multi-model routing deferred because 'the audit complexity isn't worth it yet').

External-Send QC verdict shape: the guide adds a banker-invocable rush-send override (rush mode verifies addressees only; content, codename, and metadata checks deferred and logged for supervisory review). This matches neither the Handbook's binary BLOCK with 'no human override offered at this layer' nor Vision2p's green/yellow/red re-scoring with logged yellow acknowledgment — a third distinct verdict shape for the same control.

Step count / decomposition: the guide has 65 sequenced deal steps plus 21 horizontal always-on applications (86 total), versus the canon's repeated reference to Storm's '~82 steps' model. Same idea, different decomposition and count.

Expert Panel roster: the guide's static panels (Legal & Regulatory, Product & Engineering, Process Experts, Writers/Editors/Storytellers, Persuasion & Sales, Negotiation Experts, Compliance & Risk, CCO Stand-In) plus dynamic deal-specific panels (Sector/Sub-Sector, Product-Domain, Digital Twins of the counterparty board and management, Client Psychology) differ from the canon's ten launch panels (Founders §4.4), which include Finance & Valuation, Behavioral Economics & Decision Science, Data Privacy/Security/Info Barriers, and Accounting & Financial Diligence not named in the guide, and do not include digital twins.

Team-scope tension: the guide assigns 27 numbered Operating System builds to the OS engineering team (including agentic horizontals like Sector Intelligence and MD-Style Review), versus the canon Handbook's V1 contraction in which the core team builds exactly one V1 agent (Compliance Comms PA-1) with seams only for others. The guide reads as a full build map rather than a v1 scope, and marks all assignments 'a first take — to be validated jointly', but the allocations are broader than the Handbook's.
notes: Coverage: the guide covers ALL 65 sequenced steps (Seq 1-65) with no gaps. No seq numbers are missing.

Terminology mapping: the guide calls the platform the 'Operating System (OS)' built by the 'OS engineering team' and the deal-workflow skills the 'application layer' built by RTS — corresponding to the canon's rails (Futureproofing core team) vs skills (RTS) split under different names.

Document status: working draft — 'steps may be added or removed; build responsibilities are a first take, to be validated jointly'. Companion to the Sell-Side M&A Master Process & Build Sequence, which lists every step in deal order with its build order; the 16 priority builds are marked in that companion document, not this one.
The guide references 'v9' throughout as the underlying process source it encodes (e.g. 'the checklist items come straight from v9', 'v9 adds two mandatory elements').

Regulatory wrapper: Ignatious operates through Finalis Securities LLC (Member FINRA/SIPC), the broker-dealer of record — supervision, recordkeeping, and fee collection flow through it. Everything in the guide sits inside that perimeter. Fee collection (Seq 58, 60) is explicitly routed through Finalis.

Governing rule (verbatim): 'reversible work can be automated with logs; anything irreversible, regulated, external, financial, or permission-changing requires a human approval on the record. Every class runs inside the runtime controls: per-agent budgets, step limits, loop detection, tool permissions, and a kill switch.'

No step in the guide carries execution class H (fully human); classes used are A (7 sequenced steps: Seq 4, 18, 29, 32, 35, 56, 65), A+H (majority), and H+A (Seq 6, 11, 23, 25, 28, 34, 40, 44, 48, 50, 57, 61).

OS-built steps embedded in the deal sequence (all others are RTS builds): Seq 4 Lead Registration (OS #2), Seq 6 Conflicts Checklist (OS #9), Seq 7 Codename/Deal Shell (OS #5), Seq 26 Mandate Activation Checklist (OS #19), Seq 32 Document Intake/Metadata (OS #20), Seq 43 Buyer VDR Access (OS #22). Seq 43 is explicitly 'Build Scope IN' at the OS level because it requires platform-level access control and audit infrastructure, so it is not on the Ignatious consulting-partner build list.

HORIZONTAL (ALWAYS-ON) APPLICATIONS — Part 1 of the guide defines 21 platform services available to every workflow step and every deal, not part of the deal sequence, all built at the Operating System level; the last five are newly added with provisional ordering pending joint prioritization: (1) External-Send QC (OS #1, A+H) — QC agent checks every outbound artifact for regulatory/legal/reputational compliance incl. Reg FD + FINRA 2210, codenames, addressee correctness, and hidden metadata; no external send until the responsible banker confirms; rush-send override verifies addressees only with deferred checks logged. (2) Pipeline CRM (OS #3, A) — auto-maintains the single firm-wide funnel (Live lead / Won / Lost / Hold / Terminated / Died) in HubSpot; entries scrubbed against the restricted list. (3) Work-Check (OS #4, A) — automatic second set of eyes on every primary-agent output before it reaches the banker (consistency, citations, numeric reasonableness, codename adherence, tone); advisory flags only, banker owns disposition, logged for FINRA 3110 supervisory review. (4) Sector Intelligence (OS #6, A) — continuously maintains tech-sector comps sets, precedent tables, market maps ('digiscapes'), and quadrant analyses; monthly refresh, every data point source-cited; conflict/restricted screening before pitch use. (5) Multi-Model Verification (OS #7, A+H) — 2+ alternate frontier models independently verify every consequential AI output; discrepancies diffed and severity-scored; banker resolves and owns the final output; per-deal/workspace/firm cross-check budget caps; OS partially subsidizes cross-check compute initially. (6) Expert Panel Review (OS #8, A+H) — simulated static + dynamic deal-specific expert panels red-team every consequential work product into PASS/REVISE/REWRITE; advisory only; no MNPI ever flows into digital twins, which are deal-scoped and destroyed at close. (7) Continuous Learning / Skill Optimization (OS #10, A+H) — turns completed-deal patterns, banker edits, and feedback into proposed prompt/template/weighting improvements; a partner must approve any reusable pattern; no cross-tenant training; quarterly Agent Performance Review for partner sign-off. (8) Deal Workflow Coordinator (OS #11, A) — orchestration layer on a coordinator pattern, not autonomous command; routes tasks, holds deal-state per identity triplet (Tenant:Client:Deal:User), monitors agent health/SLA, escalates blocked agents; respects identity triplet and wall status on every routing decision, no cross-deal bleed. (9) Document Retention + Permission Cross-Check (OS #12, H+A) — inventories every document with record/retention/supervisory tags; cross-checks every deletion against FINRA 4511 and SEC 17a-3/17a-4; deletion is dual-control (human approval AND regulatory check must both pass); chain-of-custody preserved. (10) License / U4 / CE Compliance Tracker (OS #13, A) — tracks banker FINRA license status, Form U4 currency, CE completion, internal certifications; alerts banker and CCO; banker-private data with CCO visibility. (11) MD-Style Review (OS #14, A+H) — applies the named MD's prior approved voice to drafts before MD review; opt-in per MD, tenant-isolated, never trains cross-MD or cross-firm, MD owns the final draft. (12) Knowledge Graph / Relationship Strength (OS #15, A) — strength-scored who-knows-whom graph from CRM/calendar/email metadata plus Pally integration; warm-path discovery; no email-content scanning by default; each banker controls visibility of their own contacts. (13) Negotiation Copilot (OS #16, H+A) — banker negotiates, agent suggests counters/justifications/anticipated responses across ELs, NDAs, LOIs, reps, escrow, earnouts; advisory only, no autonomous response to a counterparty; learns cross-firm anonymized. (14) Workflow Monitoring (OS #17, A) — opt-in Mimica/Worktrace-style instrumentation observing how bankers work; produces repetitive-pattern heat-map and agent-candidate backlog with ROI estimates; affirmative opt-in only, banker can pause/stop anytime, no individual-level HR monitoring. (15) File Storage Reorganization (OS #18, A+H) — analyzes SharePoint/Drive/iManage structure and proposes reorg options for human+AI retrieval; executes only the option a banker/partner/CCO selects; no deletions during reorg; permissions preserved; full audit trail. (16) Fee Structure Pool (OS #21, A) — pools fee structures across all OS-customer firms anonymously into percentile benchmarks by transaction type and size band; anonymization at ingestion, no firm/deal ID stored, subject to customer consent; Operating System only — not built at Ignatious; feeds the Engagement Economics agent (Seq 19). (17) Enterprise Search (OS #23, A) — permission- and barrier-aware retrieval over the firm corpus with cited sources; assembles context for other agents so no application searches from scratch; can show a document exists while withholding contents until permissioned; all queries/retrievals logged in retainable form. (18) Model Optimization (OS #24, A) — routes every task to the most cost-effective model clearing the quality bar; critique-looping on high-stakes work; token/cost tracking by user, deal, task, and agent with budget caps; approved-model list only, no client data to unapproved models. (19) Data Room Hosting (OS #25, A+H) — hosted permissioned data-room layer (Box) above SharePoint: folder taxonomy, deal/sensitivity tagging, staged buyer access, watermarking, AI-readable APIs; access changes banker-approved; buyer segregation enforced; GDPR/SOC 2 posture inherited from Box. (20) Communication Checking (OS #26, A) — Global Relay / Smarsh communications-compliance layer: captures/archives business communications, runs surveillance rules, flags exceptions to compliance/CCO; FINRA 3110 + 2210 obligations, SEC 17a-4 retention; complements External-Send QC (QC gates outbound quality; this preserves and surveils the record). (21) Staffing (OS #27, H+A) — humans make staffing decisions; agent recommends allocations from workload/skills/pipeline, flags over-allocation, wall/conflict-checks every proposed assignment; assignment history logged.
Horizontal OS build numbers span 1-27; numbers 2, 5, 9, 19, 20, 22 are the sequence-embedded OS builds listed above, so the horizontal set is #1, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 10-18, 21, 23-27.
RTS build numbers on sequenced steps run #1-59 (not in seq order — e.g. Relationship Pathing Seq 8 is RTS Build #1, Deal Pulse Seq 35 is RTS #10, League Table Submission Seq 55 is RTS #12).

A Glossary is provided at the end of the guide 'for the build team', defining sell-side terms plus the guide's own architecture terms: Operating System (platform layer — data, orchestration, governance, horizontal applications), Horizontal application (always-on platform application available to every workflow step), Application layer (deal-workflow skills built by RTS on top of the OS).
Format fields in io are null wherever the guide does not state a concrete format; the guide usually names systems rather than file formats.

Cross-check against the Master Process document itself was not performed (out of scope for this extraction); within the guide, Seq numbering 1-65 is complete and internally consistent, and the guide states it is keyed to the companion Master Process seq order.
